translationRepairs: At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously enfeoffed as bearer of the staff, grand general of agile cavalry, grand commander with the same honors as the Three Excellencies, and governor of Qing Province, with the posthumous title Gongmu.

At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously granted the titles of bearer of the staff, grand general of agile cavalry, grand commander with the same honors as the Three Excellencies, and governor of Qing Province, with the posthumous title Gongmu.
贈 here is a posthumous grant of offices and ranks, not an enfeoffment; the literal field may carry the same wording.
At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously enfeoffed as governor of Cang Province.
At the beginning of Taichang he was posthumously granted the post of governor of Cang Province.
贈滄州刺史 is a posthumous grant of the governorship, not an enfeoffment.
Later he went to Luoyang, and the Deposed Emperor made him grand commander of the central army.
Later he went to Luoyang, and Emperor Chu made him grand commander of the central army.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), who fled west, not the "Deposed Emperor" (前廢帝) mentioned earlier; the literal field may repeat the conflation.
Yanqing was both close to the Erzhu and allied with powerful sycophants; when the Deposed Emperor went west, King Xianwu of Qi entered Luoyang.
Yanqing was both close to the Erzhu and allied with powerful sycophants; when Emperor Chu went west, King Xianwu of Qi entered Luoyang.
出帝 here is Emperor Chu, who went west; rendering it "the Deposed Emperor" confuses him with 前廢帝.

At that time Chun's father Dun was still at Xiurong when suddenly there came word that Dun had died; Chun asked to reduce his own rank to posthumously enfeoff him, promoting him from General of Awesome Prestige beyond precedent to General of Chariots and Cavalry,[1] and governor of Heng Province.

At that time Chun's father Dun was still at Xiurong when suddenly there came word that Dun had died; Chun asked to reduce his own rank to have posthumous offices conferred on him, promoting him from General of Awesome Prestige beyond precedent to General of Chariots and Cavalry,[1] and governor of Heng Province.
贈 is a posthumous conferral of office, not an enfeoffment; the literal field repeats the error.
The Deposed Emperor enfeoffed Chun as palace attendant and grand commander with the same honors as the Three Excellencies.
Emperor Chu appointed Chun palace attendant and grand commander with the same honors as the Three Excellencies.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the "Deposed Emperor" (前廢帝), and 拜 means appointed, not enfeoffed.

He then secretly sowed discord, urging the Deposed Emperor to establish commanders' retainers within the palace, and also increased the number of martial guards; from attendants-in-waiting downward he appointed several hundred men, all chosen from the most reckless men in the realm.

He then secretly sowed discord, urging Emperor Chu to establish commanders' retainers within the palace, and also increased the number of martial guards; from attendants-in-waiting downward he appointed several hundred men, all chosen from the most reckless men in the realm.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).
The Deposed Emperor mustered troops at Heqiao Bridge and made Chun vanguard, encamping north of Mount Mang.
Emperor Chu mustered troops at Heqiao Bridge and made Chun vanguard, encamping north of Mount Mang.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).
Chun, fearing he could not escape, again memorialized the Deposed Emperor, using false reports of enemy movements to coerce him.
Chun, fearing he could not escape, again memorialized Emperor Chu, using false reports of enemy movements to coerce him.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).

At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was appointed left vice director of the Masters of Writing, and soon further made grand general of agile cavalry, grand commander with the same honors as the Three Excellencies, and chief rectifier of Ding Province.

At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign he was appointed left vice director of the Masters of Writing, and soon further made grand general of agile cavalry, grand commander with the same honors as the Three Excellencies, and chief rectifier of Ding Province.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).

At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was appointed regular attendant, with his existing rank, grand commander with the same honors as the Three Excellencies, and governor of Cang Province.
At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign he was appointed regular attendant, with his existing rank, grand commander with the same honors as the Three Excellencies, and governor of Cang Province.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).
In the province he was greedy and unrestrained and greatly harmed the people; the Deposed Emperor summoned him back to the capital.
In the province he was greedy and unrestrained and greatly harmed the people; Emperor Chu summoned him back to the capital.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).
In Putai, when Zihu rose to prominence, Xing was posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and governor of Jing Province.
In Putai, when Zihu rose to prominence, Xing was posthumously granted the posts of General Who Conquers the Barbarians and governor of Jing Province.
贈 is a posthumous conferral of office, not an enfeoffment.
When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Xue Xiuyi and the surrendered Shu Chen Shuangchi and others, acting under Hao's orders, led troops to attack the provincial capital.
When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Xue Xiuyi and Chen Shuangchi, who had surrendered from Shu, and others, acting under Hao's orders, led troops to attack the provincial capital.
降蜀陳雙熾 means Chen Shuangchi, a surrendered man of Shu; "Shu Chen Shuangchi" wrongly reads 蜀 as part of the name.

Emperor Zhuang approved; Zihu was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, governor of Yu Province, acting grand general of agile cavalry, commander-in-chief over the military affairs of the two Yu, Ying, and three provinces, concurrent right vice director of the Masters of Writing, and commissioner of the route for the four provinces of the two Yu, Ying, and Ying.

Emperor Zhuang approved; Zihu was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, governor of Yu Province, acting grand general of agile cavalry, commander-in-chief over the military affairs of the three provinces of the two Yu and Ying, concurrent right vice director of the Masters of Writing, and commissioner of the route for the four provinces of the two Yu, Ying (郢), and Ying (潁).
二豫郢三州 is "the three provinces of the two Yu and Ying"; the idiomatic garbles the count. 潁 and 郢 are different provinces.
On returning from the campaign the Deposed Emperor bestowed horses.
On returning from the campaign Emperor Chu bestowed horses.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).
When the Deposed Emperor entered the passes, Zihu held the city in rebellion.
When Emperor Chu entered the passes, Zihu held the city in rebellion.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).

The Deposed Emperor, having accepted the slander and discord of Hu Sichun and the others, planned against King Xianwu of Qi; because Sheng's younger brother He Bayue held troops in the Guanzhong region and he still wished to broaden his support, Sheng was appointed bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander-in-chief over the military affairs of the seven provinces of the three Jing, two Ying, Southern Xiang, and Southern Yong, grand general of agile cavalry, grand commander with the same honors as the Three Excellencies, and governor of Jing Province.

Emperor Chu, having accepted the slander and discord of Hu Sichun and the others, planned against King Xianwu of Qi; because Sheng's younger brother He Bayue held troops in the Guanzhong region and he still wished to broaden his support, Sheng was appointed bearer of the staff, palace attendant, commander-in-chief over the military affairs of the seven provinces of the three Jing, two Ying, Southern Xiang, and Southern Yong, grand general of agile cavalry, grand commander with the same honors as the Three Excellencies, and governor of Jing Province.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).
Dubo was soon killed by bandits; in the Xiaochang era he was posthumously enfeoffed as General of Pacifying the Distance and governor of Si Province.
Dubo was soon killed by bandits; in the Xiaochang era he was posthumously granted the posts of General of Pacifying the Distance and governor of Si Province.
追贈 is a posthumous conferral of office, not an enfeoffment.

When Rong entered Luoyang, for participating in the righteous enterprise he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang County with a fief of four hundred households, appointed General of the Direct Gate, and soon further made unqualified regular attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with his title advanced to General Who Pacifies the South.

When Rong entered Luoyang, for participating in the righteous enterprise he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yiyang County with a fief of four hundred households, appointed General of the Direct Gate, and soon further made unqualified regular attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with his title advanced to General Who Calms the South.
安南將軍 (advanced title) differs from the earlier 平南將軍; rendering both as "General Who Pacifies the South" makes the promotion meaningless.
At the end of the Deposed Emperor's reign an edict ordered Sheng to command troops north to the capital.
At the end of Emperor Chu's reign an edict ordered Sheng to command troops north to the capital.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).
The army halted at the Ru River; the Deposed Emperor entered the passes.
The army halted at the Ru River; Emperor Chu entered the passes.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).
Sheng's elder brother Kerni, in the Yongxi era, was Duke of Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Yan Commandery.
Sheng's elder brother Kerni, in the Yongxi era, was Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Yan Commandery.
太尉公 is the office Grand Commandant (公 marks one of the Three Dukes), not a "Duke of Grand Commandant".
At the beginning of Yong'an he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and General of Martial Guard, and granted the title Viscount of Fancheng Township.
At the beginning of Yong'an he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and General of Martial Guard, and granted the title Baron of Fancheng Township.
鄉男 is a township baron (男), not a viscount (子).
Yue secretly placed elite horsemen in separate groups of forty or fifty along the branches of water south of Weinan, posting them at intervals according to the terrain.
Yue secretly placed elite horsemen in separate groups of forty or fifty along the branches of water south of the Wei River, posting them at intervals according to the terrain.
渭南 here means the south bank of the Wei River, not the place Weinan.
Cao Ni, governor of Ling Province, came in person to Yue's army to request replacement; Yue made the former governor of Luoluo Province Yuan Jihai governor.
Cao Ni, governor of Ling Province, came in person to Yue's army to request replacement; Yue made the former governor of Luo Province Yuan Jihai governor.
洛州 is Luo Province; "Luoluo" is a duplication error.
At that time He Bayue sent Houmochen Yue ahead; Houmochen Yue then marched east through the night and on the day when light and dark met, as He Bayue's army advanced he met Houmochen Yue.
At that time He Bayue sent Houmochen Yue ahead; Houmochen Yue then marched east through the night and at dawn on the last day of the month, as He Bayue's army advanced he met Houmochen Yue.
達明晦日 means at dawn on the last day (晦日) of the month, not "the day when light and dark met".
In the sixth month he was posthumously enfeoffed as grand general, grand mentor, and recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing, with his command, governorship, and ducal title unchanged.

In the sixth month he was posthumously granted the posts of grand general, grand mentor, and recorder of the affairs of the Masters of Writing, with his command, governorship, and ducal title unchanged.
贈 is a posthumous conferral of office, not an enfeoffment.

At that time Ge Rong's separate commanders Han Lou, Hao Chang, and others had several tens of thousands of troops and were garrisoned in occupation of Ji city; Erzhu Rong ordered Yuan and Heba Sheng to campaign against them.

At that time Ge Rong's separate commanders Han Lou, Hao Chang, and others had several tens of thousands of troops and were garrisoned in occupation of Ji city; Erzhu Rong ordered Yuan and He Basheng to campaign against them.
賀拔勝 is He Basheng (surname 賀拔 Heba, given name 勝), named He Basheng elsewhere in the chapter.

Ye then enfeoffed Yuan as grand general of agile cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, governor of Ding Province, grand commander of the left army, and Duke of Yuyang Commandery with a fief of one thousand households.

Ye then appointed Yuan grand general of agile cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, governor of Ding Province, grand commander of the left army, and Duke of Yuyang Commandery with a fief of one thousand households.
授 means appointed; only the dukedom is an enfeoffment.

At the end of the Deposed Emperor's reign Yuan exchanged secret letters with Fan Zihu, governor of Yan Province, and Prince of Donglai Guiping, governor of Qing Province, to join together, and also sent secret envoys to communicate his loyalty to King Xianwu.

At the end of Emperor Chu's reign Yuan exchanged secret letters with Fan Zihu, governor of Yan Province, and Prince of Donglai Guiping, governor of Qing Province, to join together, and also sent secret envoys to communicate his loyalty to King Xianwu.
出帝 is Emperor Chu (Xiaowu), not the earlier Deposed Emperor (前廢帝).

When Emperor Chu entered the passes, Yuan again wavered and looked back.

After Prince of Ruyang Xian was removed as governor of Qi Province and halted west of the city, Yuan held his command and seized the city, not promptly welcoming and admitting him.
